user.title: Connect quicgate
user.description: First make an API token in quicgate: your account menu, **API tokens**, **New token**. Choose **Monitoring, and switch hosts on or off** to get a switch per host, or **Monitoring** to only watch. quicgate has to be version 1.19.0 or newer.

data_description.name: What this quicgate is called in Home Assistant.
data_description.url: Address and admin port, such as 192.168.1.10:81 (http unless you write https). Prefer the admin port itself over a name that quicgate proxies, so this keeps working when a proxy host is down.
data_description.token: The token is shown once in quicgate, when you make it.
data_description.verify_ssl: Only matters for an https address. Switch it off for a self-signed certificate.

full_access.title: This token can do everything
full_access.description:
The token you entered has full access. Home Assistant keeps tokens in its own storage, and whoever reads this one there can change or export your whole quicgate configuration.

A token of the kind **Monitoring, and switch hosts on or off** is enough for everything this integration does.

reauth_confirm.title: quicgate needs a new token
reauth_confirm.description: quicgate at {url} no longer accepts the token. Make a new one in quicgate (your account menu, API tokens) and enter it here.

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach a quicgate admin interface at this address.
error.invalid_token: quicgate does not accept this token.
error.too_old: This quicgate is older than 1.19.0. Update quicgate first.
error.unknown: quicgate gave an answer this integration does not understand. The Home Assistant log has the details.

switch_not_allowed.message: The API token may only watch. Make a token in quicgate that may switch hosts on or off, then connect quicgate again with it.

switch_failed.message: quicgate did not switch the host: {error}
